title: Introduce operator-scope sanitizer, KMS Shield proxy and audit fanout dispatcher
author: Priya Kaur
description:
Summary: Introduces three coordination pieces to tighten region-aware operator permissions and preserve auditable KMS usage while enabling downstream audit consumers. This PR adds: 1) an operator-scope sanitizer that enforces RBAC v2 operator allowlists and strips elevated attributes from operator-originated requests when not permitted; 2) a KMS Shield proxy that centralizes CMK selection and region pin checks with transparent retry/fallback semantics; and 3) an audit fanout dispatcher that duplicates audit events to residency-aware sinks (internal ledger + external compliance webhook) with ordering guarantees.

Motivation: Several customers requested stronger operator-scoping controls and clearer proof of KMS-residency decisions for compliance reviews (linked Linear ENG-8421). During an internal audit we found inconsistent operator headers and a handful of KMS calls missing a residency assertion. This makes post-hoc verification noisy and can require expensive manual triage. The goal is to make operator-origin assertions deterministic, ensure KMS usage is region-aware, and provide a durable, ordered audit stream for compliance consumers.

What changed: high-level code additions and config: - pkg/rbac/v2/sanitizer.go: operator-scope sanitizer logic and unit tests; enforceAllowlist(config) reads operator claims and strips disallowed attributes. - pkg/kms/proxy/shield.go: KMS Shield proxy with primary CMK selection, locale pin check, and safe fallback to customer-permitted multi-region CMKs. - internal/audit/fanout/dispatcher.go: fanout pipeline with in-order buffering and per-tenant routing. - cmd/installer/templates/kms-shield.yaml and deploy/helm/values-kms-shield.yaml: deployment defaults and feature toggle for Private installs. - docs/security/operator-scope-sanitizer.md: operator UX, migration notes, and troubleshooting tips. - tests/integration/test_kms_shield.sh: integration scenario that simulates cross-region operator and verifies audit payloads.

Compatibility & rollout: Feature gated behind config flags: rbac.operator_sanitizer.enabled and kms.shield.enabled. Default rollout is shadow mode (sanitizer logs but does not mutate) for two weeks in the canary cluster, followed by a staged enforcement rollout (tenant cohorts). KMS Shield is opt-in for Private installs via Helm value but enabled in Dedicated and Hosted clusters after signing a migration note.

Checklist: - [x] unit tests for sanitizer utilities - [x] integration test for KMS Shield happy path - [x] docs and migration guidance - [x] e2e audit verification against compliance webhook simulator - [x] security review completed

Risk & mitigation: The primary risk is unintended attribute stripping that could break operator workflows. Mitigations: shadow mode, detailed audit logs for every sanitized request, and an emergency rollback helm chart with immediate toggle of rbac.operator_sanitizer.enabled. Another risk is KMS latency introduced by the proxy; the proxy includes local caching of CMK metadata and async pre-warm of CMK handles.

Notes: This PR does not change customer-visible APIs, but it does influence how operator-originated service calls are authorized and how KMS usage is recorded for compliance. Migration steps are documented in docs/security/operator-scope-sanitizer.md and in the release notes section of this PR.
